tex_content.html:
Lemma
[the Ricci-identity substitution, metric-paired, chart-read]

↗ lem:dc-ch4-4-1 ↗ def:dc-ch4-2-1

1. ch9:2.8Let $f$ be a ($C^2$) parametrized surface read in a fixed chart and $V$ a field along it. The commutator of the two covariant derivatives, paired against a vector $w$, is the intrinsic curvature $(0,4)$ form of the chart-frame realizations of $\frac{\partial f}{\partial s}$, $\frac{\partial f}{\partial t}$, $V$ and $w$: \[ \Big\langle \frac{D}{\partial t}\frac{D}{\partial s}V - \frac{D}{\partial s}\frac{D}{\partial t}V,\ w\Big\rangle = \Big\langle R\Big(\frac{\partial f}{\partial s},\frac{\partial f}{\partial t}\Big)V,\ w\Big\rangle , \]
Proof

↗ lem:dc-ch4-4-1 \sketch The chart-level Ricci identity (section lem:dc-ch4-4-1) equates the commutator with the coordinate curvature contraction $\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{chart}}(\frac{\partial f}{\partial s},\frac{\partial f}{\partial t})V$. Pairing against $w$ and using the coordinate-to-intrinsic curvature identity rewrites the result as the intrinsic curvature $(0,4)$ form $R(\frac{\partial f}{\partial s},\frac{\partial f}{\partial t},V,w)$.

□
